Subject: POC telemetry playbook — visibility, success criteria & owners

Hi Elena / Samir —

Good to speak earlier. Per our call, attached is a concise telemetry playbook for the 6-week trial we discussed. I wanted to capture the proposed success criteria, the minimal dashboard/trace/log exports we’ll implement during the POC, and clear ownership so there’s no ambiguity when we start.

High-level ask (from Nebula): validate that Redwood meets your latency & cost profiles for the recommendation ingestion pipeline, and that the traceability + audit logs are sufficient for your compliance team.

Quick summary of what we’ll deliver during the trial (week numbers are relative to POC start):
- Week 0 (pre-deploy): config file + sample dashboards (Attachment: redwood-initial-config.yaml)
- Week 1: baseline dashboards + basic tracing enabled (low-sample)
- Week 2–3: full metrics + KV cache telemetry; log export to Nebula S3 test bucket (see links)
- Week 4: run synthetic load to validate QoS & token cost estimates; generate evaluation report
- Week 5–6: iterate on alerts, run acceptance tests, handoff eval report + SOW follow-up

Proposed POC success criteria (must-haves):
1) 95th percentile end-to-end median < 220ms for interactive recommendation calls at production-like QPS (you mentioned 50 qps target)
2) Per-request token cost within 15% of Redwood estimate (measured across 10k sample requests)
3) Error rate (5xx & timeouts) < 0.5% over a 24h window during steady-state testing
4) Request tracing usable for root-cause within 3 minutes — traces must include model_variant, request_id, route, and KV cache hits/misses
5) Logs exported to your S3 test bucket with retention metadata and PII redaction flags set (security check)

Minimal observability deliverables (we’ll provide):
- Dashboard matrix (CSV attached) mapping panels to success criteria and owners
- Pre-built Grafana dashboards: Latency (p50/p95/p99), Throughput, Error breakdown, Token cost per request, KV cache hit ratio, Model variant splits
- Tracing spans: request_received -> routing -> model_inference -> kv_cache_lookup -> response_assembly (sampling: 1% by default, adjustable)
- Log export: structured JSON logs, compressed daily, to your S3 path; include a sample schema
- Alerts we recommend: p95 latency > 300ms (warning), error rate spike > 1% (critical), token cost drift > 20% (warning)

Owners & next steps (initial):
- Alex Martinez (Sales/POC owner) — overall coordination, stakeholder syncs, SOW follow-ups
- Maya Srinivasan (Observability lead) — dashboard builds, tracing config, alert tuning
- Connor O'Brien (Infra/Deployment) — private VPC config, log export pipeline, synthetic load harness

Action requested from Nebula prior to kickoff:
- Provide an S3 test bucket path with write permissions and any data retention constraints
- Confirm the 50 qps target and a realistic request payload average token count
- Share any mandatory audit/log schema requirements (PII flags, field-level redaction)

On Sun, Feb 14, 2027 at 11:20 AM Maya Srinivasan <maya.srinivasan@redwood.com> wrote:

> Hi Elena / Alex / Samir —
>
> Quick follow-up — we can add field-level redaction in the exporter pipeline. Two implementation options:
>
> Option A (recommended, low lift): Redwood applies redaction rules at export time using a config map. We’ll redact fields named user_id, email, phone_number, and any field explicitly flagged by Nebula. This keeps your bucket safe without changing your upstream systems.
>
> Option B: Nebula applies redaction upstream, Redwood receives already-redacted logs and stores them as-is. This reduces our processing but requires you to implement redaction rules before sending.
>
> Tracing sampling: start with 1% global sampling + adaptive capture for error traces (capture 100% of traces that include 5xx or timeouts). That should give enough coverage for root-cause while keeping storage/costs low. If you want more traces for initial runs we can bump to 5% for the Week 2 baseline tests.
>
> Dashboard & metric specifics (we’ll deliver the following panels):
> - Latency: p50/p75/p95/p99, broken down by model_variant and route
> - Cost: token_cost_per_request (USD), cost_per_minute_rate (estimate)
> - Reliability: 4xx vs 5xx vs timeouts, retry counts, downstream errors
> - Cache: kv_cache_hit_ratio, cold_start_rate, cache_eviction_rate
> - Utilization: gpu_utilization, inference_concurrency, queued_requests
> - Tracing: average span duration for model_inference and kv_cache_lookup
>
> Export details: we’ll push gzipped JSON/NDJSON files to s3://nebulacorp-poc-logs/redwood/YYYY-MM-DD/ with a manifest file. Retention tags will be added; let us know the retention window you need.
>
> I’ll start scaffolding the dashboards this week and share a preview link before kickoff.
>
> - Maya
> Observability Lead | Redwood Inference
